input_reference_mode: Observed historical imagery and native references translated into prompt; no image edit target

requests.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: single Victoria 3 TECHNOLOGY illustration for a historical society research tree. This is not a flat PM pictogram, not a building scene.
Style/medium: compact hand-painted, visibly volumetric game illustration, broad painterly masses, muted natural material colors, short restrained highlights, delicate edge definition without thick dark cartoon outlines. Match the restrained painted object treatment of native Victoria 3 academia (books and diploma), democracy (torch) and political_agitation (brass speaking horn), not their subjects. No overall blue, sepia or monochrome-gold cast. No photorealism, glossy 3D render, comic sticker or cut-paper layers.
Composition: one dominant object and at most one clearly supporting accessory, centered compact silhouette on a square at least 1024x1024. Keep the complete object group inside the frame with modest fully transparent margins. Readable at 48 and 64 pixels; use large material shapes rather than excessive ornament.
Background: genuine alpha transparency outside the objects and all open gaps; all four corners completely transparent. No floor, tabletop, disc, medallion, scene, vignette background, surrounding black paint or cast-shadow patch.
Text: no readable text, no letters, numbers, dates, slogans, labels, logos, watermarks. Any visible manuscript ink consists of only faint abstract irregular horizontal strokes, not typography.
Avoid: extra props, hands, people, landscape, flags, national emblems, modern materials, UI decorations, app-icon badge, glow, neon. Output a single finished raster PNG, not a sheet of variants.
Subject: a large ivory vellum constitutional charter unrolled diagonally, gently curled at its top and bottom edges, with a small deep-red wax seal attached near its bottom. A single modest patinated gold royal crown rests at the charter's lower side, partly overlapping it; crown is clearly subordinate and no more than one third of the group. This charter-first image symbolizes written limits on sovereign power, not absolute monarchy. Treat the seal as part of the document, not an extra prop. The parchment is clean pale ivory, not yellow-brown; a few indistinct fine ink strokes only, no calligraphy or headings. Simplified historically plausible 18th-century royal crown with broad arches, no elaborate heraldic detail, giant jewels, cross or fantasy spikes. Three-quarter slightly elevated object view; matte parchment folds, subdued warm gold crown and dark red seal.

Subject: one large recognizable red wool Phrygian liberty cap, brimless, with its soft pointed crown curving FORWARD and a folded lower band. It rests atop the upper end of one short plain old wooden liberty staff, whose lower end is visible below the cap. The staff is only a compact supporting accessory, not a long spear; no metal spearhead, base, mannequin or human head. Cap dominates at least two thirds of the group. Inspired by late-18th-century revolutionary liberty-cap imagery, this is a conceptual popular-sovereignty emblem, not a replica of one nation's state insignia. Muted brick-red and burgundy cloth with clear broad soft folds and fine matte wool grain, natural brown wood. No tricolor cockade, embroidery, band inscription, Santa-hat fur or tassel. Slight three-quarter view, forward-curving tip and cloth opening clearly legible.

Subject: a thick long cream-paper petition partially unrolled, with its remaining roll clearly visible at the lower edge. The broad exposed sheet has faint abstract rows of tiny variable dark ink dashes, evoking many signatures without forming letters or readable writing. One dark brown feather quill with a cut nib lies diagonally alongside and partly across the lower sheet as the only accessory. This depicts collective petitions and coordinated reform campaigns, not a sealed private letter: NO envelope, wax seal, royal crown, liberty cap, inkwell, ribbon, loose extra sheets or megaphone. Paper is pale warm ivory with slight wear at the curled edges, not dirty sepia; emphasize the cylindrical roll and wide sheet so it is distinguishable from the flatter constitutional charter. Three-quarter slightly elevated object view; quill subordinate, no giant feather. Historically grounded in late-18th/early-19th-century public petitions, not an exact dated archival facsimile.
